row.scim_plan: Core Essentials (or Lifecycle Management add-on on Starter)
row.scim_price_text: Core Essentials: $14/u/mo (annual); add-on price not listed
row.scim_addon_price_text: Lifecycle Management add-on on Starter: price not listed (Contact Sales)
row.evidence: Okta's pricing comparison lists Lifecycle Management as an Add-on for Starter ($6) and included from Core Essentials ($14) up; Essentials ($17) lists 'Everything in Starter, plus: ... Lifecycle Management'.
row.notes: Okta is the identity provider, so this row records Okta's own SCIM provisioning (Lifecycle Management: Okta as SCIM client pushing users to downstream apps), as in June; Okta documents no inbound SCIM endpoint for provisioning users into Okta, which is done through the Users API instead. Status unchanged (gated). Changed since June: a Core Essentials suite ($14/u/mo) now includes Lifecycle Management, so the cheapest SCIM-bearing suite drops from Essentials ($17) to Core Essentials; on Starter LCM remains an add-on. June's '~$4/u/mo' add-on price has no first-party source (the pricing page shows only 'Add-on') and is dropped. All suites billed annually with a $1,500 annual minimum. sso_plan Starter means Okta's SSO product; sso_required_for_scim reflects that SCIM is added to an SSO app integration. Okta deactivates downstream users (active=false) and never sends SCIM DELETE.

plans.name: Starter
plans.notes: Lifecycle Management (SCIM provisioning) available as an add-on; price not listed.

plans.name: Core Essentials
plans.notes: Lifecycle Management included per the comparison table's check icon (icon not quotable).

scim.notes: Okta acts as the SCIM client (supports SCIM 2.0 and 1.1); the base URL is the customer's SCIM app. sso_required: SCIM is added to an existing SAML/SWA/OIDC app integration.

auth.token_source: App integration > Provisioning > Integration: Basic Auth, HTTP Header (bearer token) or OAuth2

endpoints.notes: Endpoints Okta calls on the downstream SCIM server.

deprovision.data_retained: Okta sets active=false on the downstream SCIM user; deleting the Okta user afterwards sends no DELETE to the app.

custom.how: Custom attributes in the app schema are mapped in Profile Editor and applied to the app user profile

rate_limits.text: Okta backs off and retries automatically when the downstream SCIM server returns HTTP 429, honouring Retry-After.

limitations.text: Okta never sends a SCIM DELETE for users; deprovisioning is active=false only.
Custom AIW integrations send all user updates as PUT; PATCH only for some operations on OIN integrations.
If the SCIM provisioning option is missing, Okta support must activate the feature for the org.

user_api.notes: Okta Management API (Users, Groups, User Lifecycle). No plan gate is stated in the API reference; Universal Directory is in every suite. Inbound provisioning into Okta from HR apps or other systems uses profile sourcing and this API, not an Okta-hosted SCIM endpoint.

endpoints.purpose: Delete a user (must be DEPROVISIONED; otherwise deactivates)
Assign a user to a group
Unassign a user from a group

events: user lifecycle events (e.g. user deactivation) via event hooks

rate_limits.text: Org-scoped rate-limit buckets shown in the Rate Limit Dashboard.

limitations.text: DELETE on a user that is not deactivated only deactivates it; a second DELETE is required.
Deactivation deprovisions the user from all assigned apps and can destroy app data.

okta.notes: Okta is the identity provider itself; IdP catalogue entries are not applicable.

fallbacks.other_sync: Profile sourcing from HR apps, Active Directory or LDAP into Okta Universal Directory

Whether Okta exposes any inbound SCIM endpoint for provisioning users into Okta from another IdP is not documented; framing of this row (Okta as SCIM client) should be confirmed at merge.
